evals.name: ch-headline
evals.prompt: Using Bob Bly's Copywriter's Handbook, critique and rewrite this headline for a bookkeeping service: 'Quality Bookkeeping Solutions For Your Business'. Explain the method.
assertions: Uses the four functions of a headline (attention, select audience, complete message, draw into body)
Applies the 4 U's (urgent, unique, ultra-specific, useful) with a 1-4 rating
Uses Bly's three questions (who is the customer, important features, why will they buy) or key selling proposition
Rewrites with a specific benefit (not a blind headline or pun) and offers multiple versions drawn from headline types/techniques
Avoids negatives / jargon and is specific with numbers
Mentions testing or writing several headlines / swipe file

evals.name: ch-sequence
evals.prompt: What is Bly's 'motivating sequence' for sales copy and how does it differ from AIDA? Also explain his take on USP and features vs benefits.
assertions: Lists the five steps: get attention, show a need, satisfy the need/position product, prove it, ask for action
Contrasts with AIDA (attention, interest, desire, action)
Says the headline should lead with the strongest benefit, not puns or a windup
Gives Rosser Reeves' three USP requirements (proposition/benefit; competition can't or doesn't offer; strong enough to move the mass millions)
Suggests stressing an under-publicized benefit when there is no unique feature (e.g., steam-washed beer bottles)
Explains translating features into customer benefits

evals.name: ch-email
evals.prompt: Per The Copywriter's Handbook (3rd edition), how should I structure a promotional e-mail?
assertions: Covers FROM and SUBJECT lines (FROM identifies sender; caution with 'free' and spam filters)
Lead with a strong headline/benefit up front
First paragraph is a mini-version of the whole message with offer and response link
Expanded copy follows with features, benefits, proof; repeat offer and response mechanism at close (multiple links)
Formatting/tone tips: wide margins, sparing all caps, short is generally better, helpful not hard-sell
Includes opt-out statement and/or deliverability notes; flags the 2005 edition may be dated
